cons: SaaS means prediction data leaves your infrastructure
Pricing can scale fast at high volume
Less enterprise compliance depth than IBM's offering
name: Arize AI
pros: Strong LLM tracing alongside traditional ML monitoring
files: Accepts prediction logs, embeddings, and LLM traces.
value: The practical choice for an ML team that needs model observability without the full enterprise governance stack. Handles traditional ML monitoring (drift, performance) and LLM tracing, evaluation, and prompt monitoring in one platform.
engine: Monitoring platform, not a model. Connects to model outputs and feature data.
quality: Strong on LLM tracing and evaluation, which is an area most governance platforms added late. Good ML monitoring depth.
tagline: Model observability for ML and LLM applications, used by ML teams already in production.
use_cases: Monitoring deployed ML and LLM applications for performance and data drift
Tracing LLM applications to debug prompt failures and quality issues
Running automated evaluations on LLM outputs in CI/CD
integrations: Most ML frameworks and serving platforms
LangChain, LlamaIndex, and LLM orchestration tools
CI/CD pipelines for eval in deployment
governance_note: LLM observability is the gap in most organizations' AI risk management: they monitor traditional ML models and then deploy LLM applications with no production visibility at all. A hallucination rate, a prompt injection, or a quality regression in an LLM feature is invisible without tracing. The audit question to ask is which deployed AI features have monitoring, and which are running dark.
training_optout: Monitoring platform, not a model host. Data retention and use terms govern what Arize stores from your prediction logs.
